verses.text: Here are the family heads and the family lines of those who came up with me from Babylon while Artaxerxes was king:
From Phinehas’s descendants, Gershom. From Ithamar’s, Daniel. From David’s, Hattush.
From Shecaniah’s descendants, from Parosh’s line, Zechariah, with 150 men listed with him in the family records.
From Pahathmoab’s descendants, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, with 200 men.
From Shecaniah’s descendants, the son of Jahaziel, with 300 men.
From Adin’s descendants, Ebed son of Jonathan, with 50 men.
From Elam’s descendants, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, with 70 men.
From Shephatiah’s descendants, Zebadiah son of Michael, with 80 men.
From Joab’s descendants, Obadiah son of Jehiel, with 218 men.
From Shelomith’s descendants, the son of Josiphiah, with 160 men.
From Bebai’s descendants, Zechariah son of Bebai, with 28 men.
From Azgad’s descendants, Johanan son of Hakkatan, with 110 men.
From Adonikam’s descendants, the last ones were Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, with 60 men.
From Bigvai’s descendants, Uthai and Zabbud, with 70 men.
I brought them together at the river that flows to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I looked over the people and the priests and realized there wasn’t a single descendant of Levi there.
So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, and for the teachers Joiarib and Elnathan.
I sent them to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia. I told them what to say to Iddo and his fellow temple servants there so they’d bring us people to serve at our God’s house.
Our God’s good hand was on us, so they brought us Sherebiah, a man with good judgment from the line of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel. He came with his sons and brothers, eighteen in all.
They also brought Hashabiah and, with him, Jeshaiah from Merari’s descendants, along with his brothers and their sons, twenty in all.
They brought 220 temple servants from the group David and his officials had assigned to help the Levites. Every one was listed by name.
Right there at the Ahava River I called for a fast. We wanted to humble ourselves before our God and ask him for a clear way ahead for us, our little ones, and everything we owned.

I felt ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies on the road. We’d already told him, “Our God’s hand is on everyone who seeks him, to do them good. His power and anger are against everyone who turns away from him.”
So we fasted and begged our God to help us, and he answered our request.
Then I picked out twelve of the leading priests: Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers.
I weighed out the silver, gold, and vessels for them. These were the offerings for our God’s house from the king, his advisers and officials, and all the Israelites who were there.
I handed over 650 talents of silver, silver vessels weighing 100 talents, and 100 talents of gold,
along with twenty gold bowls weighing a thousand darics and two vessels of fine, shiny bronze, as precious as gold.
I told them, “You’re set apart for the LORD, and these vessels are set apart too. The silver and gold are gifts freely given to the LORD, the God of your ancestors.
Keep watch over them until you weigh them in Jerusalem in the rooms of the LORD’s house, in front of the leading priests, the Levites, and the heads of Israel’s families.”
So the priests and Levites took charge of the weighed silver, gold, and vessels to bring them to our God’s house in Jerusalem.
On the twelfth day of the first month, we left the Ahava River for Jerusalem. Our God’s hand was on us. He rescued us from enemies and bandits along the way.
We reached Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.

On the fourth day, we weighed the silver, gold, and vessels in our God’s house and handed them to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. With him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Everything was counted and weighed, and all the weights were written down right then.

The people who’d returned from exile brought burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats for a sin offering. All this went up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
They delivered the king’s orders to his local governors and to the governors beyond the River. So those officials supported the people and God’s house.
